Let the original length be l.

In first case,

l1=l+dl1

Using Hooke's law, x=TK

Where, x is the displacement.

We have, l1=l+T1K ... (i)

Similarly, l2=l+T2K ... (ii)

What is the increment in the length (in mm) of the wire? [Young's modulus of aluminium YAl=7×1010 N m-2, sin75°≈0.97, cos75°≈0.26, g=10 m s-2]

solution.text:
The figure below shows the stone being rotated as a conical pendulum such that the wire makes an angle of 75° with the vertical. Let us assume that the radius OA of the circle is equal to r

For vertical equilibrium of the stone

Tcos75°=Mg

T=Mgcos75°

The elongation in the wire is

∆L=TLAY=MgLAYcos75°

⇒∆L=1.3×10×1.410-6×7×1010×0.26=10-3 m=1 mm

question.text: A uniform rod of length l is acted upon by a force F in a gravity-free region, as shown in the figure. If the area of cross-section of the rod is A and it's Young's modulus is Y, then the elastic potential energy stored in the rod due to elongation is

solution.text:
The acceleration of the rod is

a=Fm

So, the tension in the rod at a distance x from the free end is

Tx=mxl×Fm=Fxl

The longitudinal stress developed inside the rod at a distance x from the free end is

σ=TxA=FxlA

The strain energy density (energy per unit volume) is

dUdV=12σ2Y=12F2x2YA2l2, where dV=Adx is the volume of a small part of the rod

So the energy stored in the rod is

U=12F2YA2l2∫0lx2dx

U=F2l6A2Y

question.text:
A thin rod of negligible mass and area of cross-section 4×10-6 m2, suspended vertically from one end, has a length of 0.5 m at 100 °C. The rod is cooled to 0 °C but prevented from contracting by attaching a mass at the lower end. The value of this mass is
(Given, coefficient of linear expansion is 10-5 °C-1, Young's modulus is Y=1011 N m-2 and g=10 m s-2)

solution.text:
The change in length due to decrease in temperature,

Δl1=LαΔθ=0·510-50-100

Δl1=-0·5×10-3 m                ... (i)

Negative sign implies that length is decreasing. Now let M be the mass attached to the lower end. Then, change in length due to suspension of load is

Δl2=MgLAY=M100.54×10-61011

Δl2=1.25×10-5M           ... (ii)

Δl1+Δl2=0

⇒1.25×10-5M=0.5×10-3      (from equations (i) and (ii))

⇒M=0.5×10-31.25×10-5 kg

⇒M=40 kg

question.text: The length of an elastic string is a m  when the tension is 4 N, and 'b m when the tension is 5 N. The length in metre when the tension is 9 N, is

solution.text:
T1=Kl1-l

T2-T1l=T2l1-T1l2

l= T2l1-T1l2(T2-T1) 

l=5a-4b        .......(i)

k=1b-a            ...(ii)

question.text: The longitudinal stress in a rod (with rectangular cross-section) is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of the Young's modulus of its material. solution.text:
∵  Stress, F∆A=1% of Y=Y100 But Young′s modulus, Y=stressstrain=F∆A∆ll

∴   Y=Y100∆ll      puttingF∆A=Y100

∴  ∆ll=1100

Equivalent force constant for a wire is given by k=YAL. Because in case of a wire, F=YAL∆L and in case of spring, F=k∆x. Comparing these two, we find k of wire =YAL

keq=k1k2k1+k2=YALkYAL+k=YAkYA+Lk



∴T=2πmkeq=2πmYA+LkYAk

question.text: Two wires of diameter 0.25 cm, one made of steel and other made of brass are loaded as shown in figure. The unloaded length of steel wire is 1.5 m and that of brass wire is 1.0 m. r = 0.125 cm = 1.25 × 10-3 m

Load (F1) = (4 + 6) kgf = 10 × 9.8 N = 98 N

Length of steel wire (l1) = 1.5 m

Young's modulus (Y1) = 2.0 × 1011 Pa

Young's modulus (Y) = F 1 × l⁡ 1 A 1 × Δ l⁡ 1

Change in length Δ l⁡ 1 = F 1 × l⁡ 1 A 1 × Y 1

= F 1 × l⁡ 1 π r 1 2 × Y 1

= 98 × 1.5 3.14 × 1.25 × 10 - 3 2 × 2.0 × 10 11

​= 1.5 × 10-4 m

For brass wire,

Load (F2) = 6 kgf = 6 × 9.8 N = 58.8 N

Length of brass wire (l2) = 1.0 m

question.text: Two blocks of masses 5 kg and 10 kg are connected by a metal wire going over a smooth pulley as shown in the figure. The breaking stress of the metal wire is 2×109 N m-2. If g=10 m s-2, then what is the minimum radius of the wire which will not break

solution.text:
This is Atwood's machine. Let the tension in the wire be T and acceleration of masses a.

Then, T-5g=5a and 10g-T=10a

This gives a=13g and T⁡=203g=2003N.

Stress =T⁡area=2003×3.14×r⁡2=2×109       (given)

Thus the minimum radius r should be r=2003×3.14×2×109=1.03×10-4 m≈0.1 mm

d1d2=Y2Y1=1911

question.text: A load of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>31</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is suspended from a wire of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><mo>×</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>. question.text: There is no change in the volume of a wire due to the change in its length on stretching. The Poisson's ratio of the material of the wire is

solution.text:
Volume of cylindrical wire, V=πr2L4, where x is the diameter of wire.
Differentiating both sides,

question.text: A solid sphere made out of metal having a bulk modulus of 2×1011 Nm-2 is charged uniformly to a surface charge density σ=αε0 Cm-2, where ε0 is the permittivity of free space and α (magnitude = 1) is a positive constant of appropriate dimensions. question.text: The longitudinal stress in a rod (with rectangular cross-section) is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of the Young's modulus of its material. question.text: The pressure applied from all directions on a cube is <math><mi>p</mi><mo>.</mo></math> How much its temperature should be raised to maintain the original volume? solution.text:

⇒ ∆VV=α∆θ

∴   Volume elasticity, β=p∆V/V

=pα∆θ

⇒ ∆θ=pαβ

question.text: The edge of an aluminium cube is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> long. One face of the cube is firmly fixed to a vertical wall. A mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is then attached to the opposite face of the cube. The shear modulus of aluminium is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi>GPa</mi></math>. What is the vertical deflection of this face?

solution.text:
Given, side of a cube (l) = 10 cm  = 0.1 m

​Area its each face (A) = l2 = (0.1)2 = 0.01 m2

Load (m) = 100 kg

Tangential force acting on one face of the cube,

​F = mg = 100 × 9.8 = 980 N

Shear stress acting on this face = F A

= 980 0.01 N/m 2

= 9.8 × 104 N/m2

Shear modulus of aluminium (η)) = 25 GPa

= 25 × 109 N/m2

Shear modulus η = Shearing stress Shearing strain

or shearing strain Δ y L = Shearing stress Shear modulus

or Δ y = Shearing stress Shear modulus × L

= 9.8 × 10 4 25 × 10 9 × 0.1

= 0.392 × 10-5 m

= 3.92 × 10-7 m

question.text: Two metal strips are riveted together at their ends by four rivets, each of diameter <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext>mm</mtext></math>. or w=6.9× 10 7  4 πr 2

=6.9×4×3.14×9×10

=7.8× 10 3  N

question.text: A wire suspended vertically from one of its ends is stretched by attaching a weight of 200 N to the lower end. The weight stretches the wire by 1 mm. Then the elastic energy stored in the wire is

solution.text:
Elastic energy per unit volume = 1 2 × stress × strain

=  12×FA×ΔLL×AL

question.text: A uniform rod of length l is acted upon by a force F in a gravity-free region, as shown in the figure. If the area of cross-section of the rod is A and it's Young's modulus is Y, then the elastic potential energy stored in the rod due to elongation is

solution.text:
The acceleration of the rod is

a=Fm

So, the tension in the rod at a distance x from the free end is

Tx=mxl×Fm=Fxl

The longitudinal stress developed inside the rod at a distance x from the free end is

σ=TxA=FxlA

The strain energy density (energy per unit volume) is

dUdV=12σ2Y=12F2x2YA2l2, where dV=Adx is the volume of a small part of the rod

So the energy stored in the rod is

U=12F2YA2l2∫0lx2dx

U=F2l6A2Y

question.text: A load of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>31</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is suspended from a wire of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><mo>×</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Calculate the change in temperature of the wire if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>75</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of the stored elastic potential energy is converted into heat. The Young's modulus and heat capacity of the material of the wire is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mo>×</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>10</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>490</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>kg</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> respectively.

options.text: 4.33 × 10-2 K
8.33 × 10-3 K
2.44 × 10-5 K
6.22 × 10-2 K

solution.text:
As work done in stretching an elastic body per unit volume is given by

      W V = 1 2 stress × strain = 1 2 stress 2 Y      as Y = stress strain      ........ (1)

So         W = 1 2 Mg A 2 V Y            as stress = F A = Mg A

Now according to given problem heat produced H = (75/100)  W = 3 4 .W

              ⇒   ms Δ θ = 3 4 × 1 2 Mg π r 2 2 V Y           as H = ms Δ θ using equation (1)

or          ρ V s Δ θ = 3 4 × 1 2 Mg π r 2 2 V Y         as m = ρ V

∴       Δ θ = 3 8 3 1 . 4 × 9 . 8 π × 1 0 - 6 2 1 9 . 8 × 1 0 1 0 × 1 9 × 1 0 3 × 4 9 0

i.e.,  Δ θ = 1 1 2 0 K = 8 . 3 3 × 1 0 - 3  K
